title: Accuracy of a restricted Fourier weight estimate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube, let $\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\leq1$, and let $W$ assign a rational number $W(J,S)$ to every subset $J$ of the coordinates and every subset $S\subseteq J$. The estimate is accurate if, for every such $J$ and $S$, its error in estimating the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on $J$ at $S$ is less than $\tau^2/4$; that is, $|W(J,S)-\widehat W_f(J,S)|<\tau^2/4$, where $\widehat W_f(J,S)$ denotes that restricted Fourier weight.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
$W(J,S)$ is rational for every coordinate subset $J$ and every $S\subseteq J$
The error bound holds for every $J$ and every $S\subseteq J$
